C-RELEASE-SIGN-STAGED-SET.IntentSummary: Repair the two execution defects that make the C-RELEASE-SIGNING-SPLIT staged handoff fail the release lane on every run, and close the test gap that let them through. D1 (macOS): the sign job's verify step copies the staged set into /tmp/release (:984-985), so the UNSIGNED staged DMG already occupies /tmp/release/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg when "repackage and notarize the staged DMG" (:1113-1132) runs hdiutil convert "$RW_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_DST" (:1130) onto that exact path — hdiutil convert refuses an existing output (exit 1, reproduced on a real Mac) and the step runs under set -euo pipefail, so macOS signing dies every run. Fix: convert into the sign work dir (SIGNED_OUT="$APP_WORK/Mark_${VER}_aarch64.dmg"), then replace the destination atomically (mv -f "$SIGNED_OUT" "$DMG_DST"), with a one-line comment naming the reason; notarize and staple keep consuming "$DMG_DST"; the fresh-receipt re-emit loop stays. D2 (Windows): the smoke screenshot is saved inside the staged dir ($env:RUNNER_TEMP\release\app-screenshot.png :797 — STAGE_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/release" :837/:867), the stage step receipts only the exe (echo "$HASH" > "$EXE_DST.sha256" :881) so latest-platform.json (:846) is always staged without a receipt, and the wildcard uploads (${{ runner.temp }}\release\* :909, :1281) carry the unreceipted files to the sign job, whose Windows verifier (:1013-1047) refuses every run with [ReleaseSign][sign][BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH]. Fix: the screenshot moves to $env:RUNNER_TEMP\smoke (directory created first; nothing else reads it from the old path — the only other app-screenshot.png matches in the tree are frozen historical release-asset names in docs/release-notes/github-releases-archive.json and untracked local review artifacts); the Windows stage step gains a receipt loop over the staged dir (for STAGED in "$STAGE_DIR"/*; do with the existing node sha256 one-liner, skipping *.sha256), mirroring the macOS loop (:736-741); both Windows uploads name their files as path: lists (the macOS lanes' existing style) — staged: the exe, its .sha256, latest-platform.json and its .sha256; signed: those plus the .exe.bundle; the .sig drops from the signed set exactly as the macOS list already drops it (no downstream consumer reads it — prepare-publication's Windows copy_one list :1365 names exe/.sha256/.bundle and the feed merge :1328 reads latest-platform.json only); artifact names unchanged. D3: tests/renderer/release-governance.test.js pins the digest guard only on the macOS step (sign.body.indexOf('- name: verify staged artifact digests') :291 matches the macOS step first) and nothing executes the workflow's shell — extend the requireVerifyThenSign block (:288-306) so BOTH verify steps are located, sliced and held to the same demands (a mutation of EITHER step is rejected, red controls added to the existing in-memory mutation test), and add the comment-blind CRLF-tolerant validator assertSignStagedHandoff with a positive pin test (keeps the staged handoff collision-free and fully receipted) and a red-control test (fails closed on in-memory mutations of the sign staged handoff). Execution gate (decision 4): tests/tools/sign-staged-handoff.test.mjs — vitest, Node-only (first-line @vitest-environment node pragma, the tests/tools precedent for subprocess-driving suites under the lane's globally configured jsdom), no new dependencies, no network — parses release.yml with the lockfile yaml package and EXECUTES the extracted run: shells with bash against synthetic staged directories: both verify loops on every OS (pass: file+receipt exits zero; missing receipt exits nonzero with BLOCK_SIGN_DIGEST_MISMATCH; tampered bytes exit nonzero); a stage-then-verify case running the extracted Windows stage script over a staged dir holding the exe and latest-platform.json and demanding the verifier pass — red on the current text, green after the fix; the repackage case only where hdiutil exists (explicit skip reason elsewhere) against a tiny real hdiutil-created disk image with xcrun/codesign/spctl PATH shims — red on the current text (occupied destination), green after the fix. The extracted workflow text is the only place /tmp/release exists: the gate applies exactly ONE declared substitution — the literal /tmp/release becomes a per-test temporary directory under the OS temp root, failing loudly when a step expected to contain it does not — so the collision semantics are exercised without ever touching a fixed shared path; cleanup happens only inside the per-test temp directory in a finally block, including detaching any mounted image. The gate lands FIRST, deliberately red, and the workflow fix flips it green.
